predecessors.name: Brythons (Celtic Britons)
predecessors.text: the British lands on the lower Severn and Cotswolds, where Wessex killed three British kings at Deorham in 577

successors.name: Kingdom of Mercia
successors.text: Mercia's 628 shape, which grows by 10,350 km2 over its 617 shape and includes the Hwicce

ledger.x: 577: the kingdom of the Hwicce is established after the West Saxon victory at Deorham.
587: the Hwicce reach south toward Bath.
628: the Hwicce become a Mercian client.

wars.name: Battle of Deorham
wars.outcome: '577: Here [Cuthwine] and [Ceawlin] fought against the Britons, and they killed 3 kings, Coinmail, Condidan and Farinmail' and 'took 3 cities: Gloucester and Cirencester and Bath'; a Saxon victory at Dyrham, a few miles north of Bath.

wars.name: Battle of Cirencester
wars.outcome: 'Cynegils and Cwichelm fought against Penda at Cirencester and then came to an agreement'; 'Penda took over the Severn Valley in 628', and the Hwicce became a client of Mercia.

certainty.note: Tribal frontiers known from later diocesan and shire boundaries; no source fixes a line.
